prompt.text: Which DNA nucleotide will be replaced by Uracil (U) in RNA?

questions.explanation: RNA uses uracil (U) in place of thymine (T); A, G, and C pair similarly in both nucleic acids.

prompt.text: DNA strands are held together by what type of bonds between nucleotides?

questions.explanation: Complementary base pairs are linked by hydrogen bonds; the sugar–phosphate backbone uses covalent bonds.

prompt.text: An atom with a negative charge is called a(n):

questions.explanation: An anion is a negatively charged ion; a cation is positively charged.

prompt.text: True or false: The number of protons and electrons in an atom are not always equal, but the number of protons and neutrons is always equal.

questions.explanation: Neutral atoms have equal protons and electrons, but proton and neutron counts need not be equal (isotopes vary in neutrons).

prompt.text: True or false: Isotopes are always radioactive.

questions.explanation: Many isotopes are stable; only some are radioactive.

prompt.text: Covalent bonds form when electrons are ___.

questions.explanation: Covalent bonds form by sharing electron pairs between atoms.

prompt.text: True or false: All covalent bonds are polar.

questions.explanation: Nonpolar covalent bonds occur when electronegativity is similar (e.g., C–H); not all covalent bonds are polar.

prompt.text: True or false: Molecules can contain a mixture of polar and nonpolar covalent bonds.

questions.explanation: A molecule can include both polar regions (for example, O–H) and nonpolar regions (for example, hydrocarbon chains).

prompt.text: True or false: Ionic bonds always form a cation and an anion.

questions.explanation: Ionic bonding transfers electrons, producing a positively charged cation and a negatively charged anion.

prompt.text: If an atom of Na (atomic number 11) bonds with an atom of chlorine (atomic number 17), how many electrons will Na have after bonding?

questions.explanation: Na (11 electrons) loses one electron to Cl, leaving 10 electrons (Na+).
